messages.subject: Stats.select error and a question about detection rates
messages.subject_clean: Stats.select error and a question about detection rates
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have one question about an error I've been unable to resolve and a second question about detection rate. First, we’ve conducted a series of simulations evaluating hair snare trap design for black bears. For a given simulation, we want to extract statistics on three estimated parameters (D, g0 and sigma). The following code successfully extracts the statistics for density (D):

stats1 <- select.stats(sim.d1, parameter = "D", statistics = c("estimate", "lcl", "ucl", "RB", "RSE", "COV"))

However, when we replaced "parameter = " with "g0" or "sigma", we received the following error: Error in scenario[, param] : incorrect number of dimensions

 "find.param()" successfully identifies D, g0, and sigma and we can see the estimates have been calculated but for some reason we can't extract them.

1)      Secondly, is it possible to extract estimates of the detection rate and locations of each detection? I realize it's possible these are being calculated mathematically rather than producing actual estimates, but I wanted to double check!

T   Thank you so much for any suggestions!

S

J    Jennifer

messages.subject: Re: Stats.select error and a question about detection rates
messages.subject_clean: Stats.select error and a question about detection rates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jennifer

As a first step to sorting this out - are you using conditional likelihood (CL = TRUE)? Then I think the default extractfn uses derived(), which leaves behind the estimates of g0 and sigma...

I'm not quite clear what you mean by 'detection rate and the locations of each detection'. If this is a query about the raw data generated by each simulation, before model fitting, then you could try fit = FALSE.

Murray

messages.subject: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
messages.subject_clean: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
messages.body_plain:
I have just started using secr and have two questions about it. My data is the following;

I have vole capture-mark-recapture data from 1983-2015. Trap sessions were in August from 1983-2015 (Totally 52 sessions). Traps were set in 5 consecutive days in the first week of the month (5 occasions in each session). Voles were checked about their sex, age (juvenile or adult), and weight as individual covariates. Environmental covariates (session-specific covariates) were seed abundance of last year (for density).

My questions are the following;

1) Zero record session
In 2002, we did set traps in every occasion, but could not capture any only in the year. Although I would like to evaluate that no record with environmental covariates, I do not know how to incorporate that into read.caphist.

2) Double hcov?
As individual covariates, I have age (juvenile and adult) and sex (male and female). Both have missing values, so I wanted to put these two into hcov at the same time. Does anyone have an idea for this issue?

Sincerely,
Ryo

messages.subject: Re: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
messages.subject_clean: Questions about session-specific covariate and hcov
messages.body_plain:
Hi
1. There is a mechanism for this: include a 'dummy' capture record for the session (with any occasion and trapID), using NONE as the animalID (you can change this with the 'noncapt' argument of read.capthist). At least, that is supposed to work, but I haven't tried it for a long time. This is part of the code that doesn't get much testing, so please
get back to the list if you find 'zero-captures' sessions don't behave as you expect.
2. Unfortunately, I don't have an elegant solution. hcov really only works with a 2-class mixture. You could try age then sex in different models. Or drop captures with missing values (if there aren't a lot) and treat age and sex as individual covariates (use CL = TRUE).
Murray

messages.subject: SECR training workshops
messages.body_plain:
I and colleagues from the University of St Andrews will be putting on a 3-day SECR workshop in St Andrews, Scotland, in August, and a one-day SECR workshop attached to the ISEC conference in Seattle in June. Deatils below.

Instructors: David Borchers, Ben Stevenson (Seattle & St Andrews) and Eric Rexstad (St Andrews only)

Content: The workshops have overlapping content, but different duration (hence intensity), with the St Andrews workshop including analyses of participants' own data, and the Seattle workshop involving example datasets only.

The workshops will cover the key concepts underlying SECR methods, and provide training in use of the methods. They will cover binary, count and time-to-detection data types, and all kinds of detectors, including camera traps, hair snares, acoustic detectors, mist nets and single-catch traps, and transect and area searches. Participants will get hands-on training in estimating density, abundance and related parameters.  Issues of measures of precision and model selection will be discussed.  Use of SECR with spatially-referenced variables for generating predictions of animal density and habitat use across landscapes will be covered.

Training workshop in Seattle 26 June 2016.  One day workshop held immediately prior to the International Statistical Ecology Conference on the campus of the University of Washington.  The workshop will introduce participants to SECR methods ranging from the most basic to the most recently developed.  Some example analyses (using R) will be conducted during the workshop.

Further information and registration details for Seattle workshop can be found at

http://depts.washington.edu/uwconf/wordpress/isec2016/workshops/

Training workshop in St Andrews 29-31 August 2016.  Target audience is biologists/ecologists who intend to, or are currently using spatial capture-recapture methods for the estimation of abundance/density/distribution.  The workshop will be hands-on, primarily using the R package 'secr', although mention will be made of other software.  Participants are encouraged to bring their own data formatted for use by 'secr' or 'admbsecr' (primarily for acoustic data). Familiarity with the R language is assumed and will be aided with pre-workshop online tutorials.

Further information and registration details for St Andrews workshop can be found at
http://creem2.st-andrews.ac.uk/spatial-capture-recapture-workshop-29-31-august-2016/
